claim: The amygdala is a highly connected cluster of nuclei with input from multiple sensory modalities and vast projections to distributed cortical and subcortical regions involved in autonomic regulation and cognition.
source: The amygdala is a highly connected cluster of nuclei with input from multiple sensory modalities and vast projections to distributed cortical and subcortical regions involved in autonomic regulation and cognition (Kim et al., 2011; McDonald and Mott, 2017; Roy et al., 2009; Stein et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research

claim: The amygdala has the capacity to facilitate the encoding of long-lasting emotional memories.
source: Numerous studies have described the amygdala's capacity to facilitate the encoding of long-lasting emotional memories (Dolcos et al., 2004; Hermans et al., 2014; LaBar and Cabeza, 2006; Phelps, 2006; Phelps, 2004; Phelps and LeDoux, 2005; Qasim et al., 2023; Richardson et al., 2004; Roozendaal et al., 2009; Schwabe et al., 2013; Zheng et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by numerous citations to prior research

claim: Specific oscillatory dynamics in the amygdalohippocampal circuit are essential in prioritizing the encoding of salient memories.

evidence: Supported by citations to recent research

claim: Direct electrical stimulation of the basolateral complex of the amygdala in humans can enhance declarative memory irrespective of emotional valence.

evidence: Supported by citation to prior research by the authors' group

claim: BLA stimulation likely enhances memory by promoting synaptic plasticity-related processes underlying memory consolidation in the hippocampus and medial temporal lobe.
source: Recently, direct electrical stimulation of the basolateral complex of the amygdala (BLA) in humans has revealed a more generalized ability to enhance declarative memory irrespective of the emotional valence (Inman et al., 2018), likely by promoting synaptic plasticity-related processes underlying memory consolidation in the hippocampus and medial temporal lobe (McGaugh, 2013; McGaugh, 2004; McGaugh et al., 2002; Roesler et al., 2021).
evidence: Inferred mechanism supported by citations to prior research

claim: Theta burst stimulation is known to induce long-term potentiation, a key mechanism in memory formation.

claim: Intracranial TBS may enhance memory specificity.
